summary:
MARS-SURVIVOR (ARES-3) is an interactive, browser-based Mars exploration support system developed to improve the safety and efficiency of future astronaut missions. It combines Martian terrain mapping, scientific data visualization, intelligent route planning, resource estimation and an AI-powered survival assistant.

The project addresses the challenges of Mars exploration, such as dangerous slopes, radiation exposure, dust storms, limited resources and communication difficulties. Using the AI pathfinding algorithm, it calculates suitable routes while considering terrain difficulty. It also provides environmental hazard maps, travel distance and resource estimates, elevation profiles, and AI-based assistance through ARES-3.

This project is important because it demonstrates how artificial intelligence and modern web technologies can support safer mission planning, better decision-making and more efficient planetary exploration. It aims to contribute towards making future human missions to Mars safer and smarter.
details:
MARS-SURVIVOR (ARES-3) is a browser-based Mars exploration support prototype designed to help plan safer and more efficient astronaut surface missions. It combines interactive Martian terrain visualization, hazard mapping, route planning, resource estimation and an AI-powered assistant in one interface.

The system uses the AI pathfinding algorithm to identify routes while considering terrain difficulty. Users can explore four Martian locations: Jezero Crater, Olympus Mons Caldera Rim, Valles Marineris Rift Valley and Gale Crater (Mount Sharp). The interface includes scientific overlays for terrain, slope hazards, radiation, potential subsurface water ice and communication coverage. It also provides route distance, elevation information and estimated resource requirements. A dynamic dust-storm simulation demonstrates how changing environmental conditions could affect mission planning. The ARES-3 assistant uses Google's Gemini API to provide AI-based assistance.

The project aims to demonstrate how web technologies, pathfinding and artificial intelligence can support better situational awareness and decision-making during future Mars exploration. Its creative approach is to combine several mission-planning concepts into an accessible interactive browser application.

The prototype was developed using HTML5, CSS, JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, Tailwind CSS, the A* algorithm and Google's Gemini API. Key considerations included astronaut safety, terrain difficulty, environmental hazards, limited resources, communication challenges, usability and future expansion. It is an educational prototype, not a certified NASA mission-control or flight system.
